basics.name: Rishabh Jain
basics.label: Technical Project Manager
basics.tagline: Engineer first, then government consultant, now project manager: 11+ years taking national platforms and enterprise portfolios from the first meeting to go-live.
basics.headline: Project Manager  |  Government and enterprise digital platforms  |  Delivery, governance and AI scoping
basics.summary: Project Manager with 11+ years in IT: software engineering first, then government consulting, now project and programme management. Owns delivery end to end (scope, schedule, budget, risk, vendors and people) on national government platforms and enterprise application portfolios, from requirements to go-live and beyond. Holds fixed dates by re-planning early, runs governance across organisations that do not report to each other, and keeps AI advisory, evidenced and accountable. Open to project and programme manager roles, including AI programmes.

work.name: BDO India
highlights: Own delivery of two concurrent national government platforms end to end: scope, schedule, budget, risk, vendors and teams of eight and ten.

Took a statutory commission's case-management platform from kick-off to go-live in about a month, against a date fixed in law, across four organisations with no reporting line, by cutting the plan from five sprints to two and running modules in parallel.
Replaced the commission's spreadsheet with an auditable, role-based workflow sized for ten times its launch volume; daily case intake rose about twentyfold.

Led a multi-crore national clean-energy certification platform from the first client meeting to public launch on its fixed date, defining a first-of-its-kind process with the ministry and baselining about 250 features across 11 modules before sprint one.
Ran governance on both: weekly steering, daily stand-ups, director-level milestone reviews, monthly reporting, formal change control and a defined escalation path.
Took both platforms through external security audits before launch; on the certification platform an internal review closed over 90% of findings first, so the audit needed one short round of fixes.
Scoped the Phase 2 AI layer for both as advisory only, with a named officer accountable for every decision; one is approved and in procurement.

work.name: Infosys
highlights: Owned the P&L, delivery and a 35-person team on a $2M+ a year portfolio of about 55 applications, holding the Project Manager, Product Owner and Scrum Master roles.
Took a loss-making unit to about 15% profit in six months by fixing how the work was organised before reducing headcount.
Held 99.9% service levels on 24x7 systems and cut the time to fix a production issue from 4 days to under 12 hours.
Turned out-of-scope work that had been delivered free into separately scoped, paid work worth about $200,000 a year.
Brought AI into ticket routing and closure in evidence-gated stages; it reached production and was never rolled back.

work.name: EY India
highlights: Moved a national regulatory registry from a paper-based office to a live platform for 40 million members; application processing became more than 70% faster.
Found that the governing statute, not the technology, was the blocker and proposed the amendments that made electronic notices and digital signatures valid; they were enacted in about six months.
Wrote the DPR and RFP for a multi-crore national citizen-services portal, onboarded the vendor and ran a second procurement for machine translation.
Held vendors to agreed scope from the client side through deviation management, change control and escalation.

Project-managed a 150+ parameter national benchmarking framework for government websites with academic research partners, and moved 80+ government websites onto one framework with security audits and standards certification.
Redesigned a national immigration services platform across air, land and sea ports of entry, and managed the consultant team delivering it.

work.name: UST Global
highlights: Led an enterprise blockchain credentialing platform from requirements with four user groups to a unit-wide pilot, where about 80% of people joined voluntarily; cut an NFT marketplace from scope to protect the core platform.

work.name: ValueCoders
highlights: Built backend and blockchain systems for a cryptocurrency exchange, a document-management platform and a civil records platform, including the architecture, APIs and performance fixes.

work.name: Tata Consultancy Services
highlights: Automated a manual card-dispute reconciliation on a bank mainframe, saving about GBP 200,000 a year by the client's own calculation, and cut reported defects by 40%.
Built blockchain proofs of concept on Ethereum and Hyperledger Fabric; two reached production.
